name: Art Nouveau tiles
region: Britain, Belgium, France, Germany and Austria
summary: Moulded earthenware tiles with a plant line in low relief and a deep, soft glaze. The tile joins a flowing stem, a lily or a woman's hair to a sea-green or plum ground. Factories made them for shop fronts, stairs, hearths and tube stations.

philosophy.core_thesis: A factory tile can carry the line of a plant, if the mould and the glaze do the drawing.
design_principles: Draw the design as one curved line, thicker at the base and thin at the tip, that flows across 2 to 4 tiles.
Press the line in low relief of 1 to 3 mm, so that the glaze pools in the hollows.
Use a matt or satin glaze with a soft break in colour at each edge of the relief.
Choose muted colours: sea green, plum, ochre, grey blue and cream, with 2 or 3 in one panel.
Make the tile 6 inches square or a tall panel, and plan a border and a frieze for the same line.
Use a motif from nature: lily, iris, poppy, peacock feather, or a woman with long hair.
Apply the colour in thick pools, or draw each line with a trail of slip, so that each colour keeps to its field.
Set the tiles in hearths, porches, stair risers and shop fronts, where the line leads the eye.
anti_patterns: A straight geometric grid in the Gothic manner
A sharp black outline with flat poster colour
A glossy single-colour glaze with no relief
A heavy gilt frame around each tile
A photographic print on a flat tile

form.shape: Square wall tiles, tall panels, hearth and fireplace tiles, friezes, and stair risers.
form.profile: A flat tile with a low modelled relief of 1 to 3 mm; the relief edges are soft and rounded.
form.foot_and_rim: The back is ribbed for the mortar; the edge is square and the glaze stops at the arris.
form.proportion: A tile is 6 inches square, or 6 by 12 inches for a frieze; a panel joins 2 to 6 tiles.
rules: Let the main line cross the joint between tiles.
Keep the relief low so that the tile stacks and the glaze does not run off.
Fix 3 or 4 glaze colours for a design, and keep each to its area.

bodies.rule: Use a white or buff earthenware that presses well in a plaster mould and takes a soft glaze. Keep porcelain and stoneware out.

methods: pressing the tile from dust in a steel die
making a plaster master from a drawn design
pouring a thin trail of slip along the line
dipping the tile in a coloured glaze
wiping the high relief by hand
forming.joins: Tiles are set in cement on a wall or a hearth, and the line is planned across the joint.
forming.details: A soft pool of glaze in each hollow, a thin break on each edge of the relief, and a pottery mark on the back.

glaze.pattern: A curved plant line in low relief; one or two soft glaze colours pool in the hollows and break on the high points.
glaze.wear: The relief edge is the first to wear and shows the pale body; the pools of glaze stay deep for decades.

palette.strategy: Muted sea and plant tones with one warm accent; the break of the glaze gives the second tone of each colour.

firing.kiln: A coal-fired or gas muffle kiln, with the tiles in saggars.
firing.scale: Factories pressed tiles by the thousand in a day, and the same line could go into a thousand hearths.
firing.signs: Soft pools of glaze, a thin break at the edge of the relief and clean, square edges.

positive: still-life museum photograph, soft north light

Relief-moulded hearth tiles with plant stems

evidence.title: Art Nouveau wall tiles, Bouillon Racine, Paris

emotion.target_response: A calm, living curve: the viewer feels a garden in the room and a little wonder at the line.

use_cases: a hearth or porch in the Art Nouveau style
a shop front or stair in plant relief
a museum label on a moulded tile
avoid_when: the brief needs a strict geometric floor
the brief needs a plain white wall
the brief needs a modern large format

modifiers.how: Remove the relief, use a white gloss glaze, and set the tiles in a brick bond.
